_comment: Single provider-routing policy shared by promptcraft, execution-orchestrator, cascade-dispatch, dm-review, assess, and research. Keep task-fit decisions here so provider routing does not drift across plugin docs.

subscriptionFirst.invariant: subscription rails first while live headroom clears the threshold for BOTH the weekly cap and the 5-hour window; API rails next by quality-per-price from the model matrix; never start planned multi-chunk work that projected spend would push below threshold mid-run
subscriptionFirst.headroomSource: usage-probe.sh live probe; a subscription rail is available only when its record is well-formed, state is exactly ok, and numeric remaining_pct is above the threshold. Unknown, missing, malformed, at-threshold, limited, and low subscription readings are unavailable. OpenRouter is an auto-reloading API balance rail: it is available only when state is exactly ok and balance_usd is a finite non-negative number; it has no legacy $5 minimum.

operatorProfile.precedence: The profile may RANK and REMOVE only among policy-derived routing options; it never adds a routing provider the derivation did not find, and never overrides neverOfferable, security invariants, or the family-independence rule. Declaring a subscription rail is NOT adding a routing option: a profile entry supplies observability only -- which windows a rail has and how to probe its headroom. A declared rail becomes eligible to route only if policy derivation already found that provider; if it did not, the entry still yields headroom readings and still routes nothing.
operatorProfile.precedenceRef: operator-profile-schema.json properties.precedence -- the tracked definition of remove-only precedence
operatorProfile.absence: No profile present means policy defaults and today's behavior.
operatorProfile.subscriptionSet: Open for OBSERVABILITY only: declare a new subscription rail with one profile entry, its windows, and its probe argv, and usage-probe.sh will report that rail's headroom with no contract edit. That alone can NEVER make the rail routable -- adding a routing option still requires a policy-ladder or derivation change, per precedence above. A profile entry for a provider the derivation did not find yields headroom readings and routes nothing.
operatorProfile.probeResolution: Use the built-in probe for a known rail, otherwise the profile-declared probe, otherwise unknown. Every profile probe runs under usage-probe.sh's reset PATH and must map to the common state, remaining_pct, and window shape; unmappable output is unknown.
operatorProfile.dataBoundary: Profiles carry preferences and probe commands only, never credentials or account secrets.
operatorProfile.consumerStatus: usage-probe.sh consumes .subscriptions only -- it executes each rail's probe and emits headroom. familyPreferenceOrder and neverUse are validated for shape but are NOT yet read by any executable consumer: cascade-dispatch.sh selects rails from the policy ladder and does not load this profile. Until a selection-time consumer exists, a profile can shrink or reorder nothing at runtime, and an operator MUST NOT assume neverUse removes a provider from dispatch. The declared contract is the target shape; this field records how much of it is live, so the gap is visible rather than implied.
operatorProfile.probeExecution: A profile probe is an argv ARRAY, never a shell string, and is executed without sh -c: no metacharacters, word splitting, globbing, or chaining. probe[0] must resolve on the reset PATH or be an absolute path to an executable regular file. A git-TRACKED profile is refused outright, because .gitignore is defeated by git add -f in this repository and a committed profile is not developer-local config. Symlinked profiles are refused.

targets.rationale: Coding-only calibration: subscriptionProfiles[activeSubscriptionProfile] is the sole target. Codex Pro 20x uses 65/0/35 Codex/Claude/OpenRouter; switching to codex-5x uses 40/0/60. Claude is non-coding-only and therefore has zero coding share. Apply the target as routing pressure only among eligible chunks; security and required live-tool capabilities remain authoritative and their exclusions must be receipted. DeepSeek V4 usage is counted under OpenRouter.

chunkKind._comment_kinds: config/docs/mechanical-logic/logic/ui/integration are ROUTING buckets, not manifest kind enum values. The manifest kind enum stays {ui, logic, integration, config}; docs and mechanical-logic are refinements carried by the manifest `executor` field (derived from kind + estimatedComplexity per manifest-schema.md Executor Mapping), not first-class kinds. model-cascade.class_from_kind bridges only the manifest kinds (logic/config/docs/ui/integration); mechanical-logic routes via `executor: openrouter` set at prompt-generation time, so it needs no class_from_kind entry.

config.rationale: Docs, receipts, JSON/YAML/TOML, and pure-prose edits fit cheap large-context text models.

docs.rationale: Documentation generation and cleanup is text-heavy and usually low visual-risk.

mechanical-logic.rationale: Rename follow-through, test tables, seed data, and migration edits are bounded mechanical code changes.

logic.rationale: Complex service and handler logic uses Codex agentic coding with OpenRouter fallback.

ui.rationale: UI implementation and code review use Codex with browser evidence; Claude is reserved for non-coding work.

integration.rationale: Cross-chunk wiring and route verification use Codex, with OpenRouter fallbacks and no Claude coding rung.

pattern-recognition-specialist.rationale: Pattern checks use low-cost Luna on the OpenRouter rail, then GLM-5.2, before Codex fallback.

code-simplicity-reviewer.rationale: Simplification review uses low-cost Luna, then GLM-5.2, before Codex fallback.

doc-sync-reviewer.rationale: Documentation consistency uses OpenRouter large-context models at any diff size.

test-coverage-reviewer.rationale: Coverage gap detection is read-heavy and uses the OpenRouter mechanical ladder.

openrouter-bulk-analyst.rationale: Bulk/large-context analysis keeps Kimi K3 primary for provider diversity, with Terra then Codex as capacity fallbacks.

security-auditor-openrouter.rationale: Kimi K3 analyzes only content-boundary-eligible sections; full or partial declines are completed under this same logical lane on Codex.

security-auditor-codex-signoff.rationale: Independent full-diff security completion is mandatory. The stable lane id does not select Codex when Codex implemented the diff.

architecture-reviewer.rationale: Architecture code review is Codex-native; Claude is non-coding-only.

assessFanout.rationale: Assessment fan-out is read-heavy summarization; keep final synthesis on Claude.

researchFanout.rationale: Research fan-out is read-heavy summarization; keep final synthesis on Claude.

adversarialReview.rationale: Default adversarial review uses two non-Claude lenses; Claude plan-adversary is an optional third lens or tiebreak.

exhaustionFallback._comment: Fires when every rail permitted for a chunk is exhausted or gated (cascade RC 76). The current ask can wait or park only. Executable fallback authorization is unavailable until trusted host authority can issue and consume a replay-resistant single-use capability. PIPELINE_EXHAUSTION_ASK=0 restores the hard block for headless CI.
exhaustionFallback.offerableDerivation: none until trusted host authority exists; live rail status is still shown to inform wait versus park
neverOfferable: every executable fallback provider until trusted single-use host authority exists
exhaustionFallback.operatorOverride: optional file OUTSIDE the workspace may narrow the derived list (per-developer subscriptions differ). It is applied LAST in the ask-time derivation and can only REMOVE options: an entry it names that the derivation did not find is ignored rather than added, and nothing in neverOfferable is ever reachable through it. Its annotations are never rendered into the ask. It must not live in the workspace, because a prior chunk's own output could rewrite an in-workspace file to strip every option but the orchestrator itself.
exhaustionFallback.failClosed: a missing routing-policy.json, a missing or malformed exhaustionFallback, or any mode other than ask restores the old hard block; no configuration read failure yields a path to fallback
exhaustionFallback.authorization: future design only; caller-owned receipts authorize nothing until a trusted host issuer binds and consumes a replay-resistant capability for the ask, repository, run, chunk, provider, phase, and attempt
exhaustionFallback.liveStatusRequired: the ask shows the derived status per rail (capped-until / available / unknown) so the operator decides from live facts; where usage-probe parsers are TODO stubs the ask says unknown rather than guessing
exhaustionFallback.rationale: The provider boundary forbids silent or caller-authorized fallback. The current ask supports wait or park; future executable fallback requires trusted host authority.

providerOrigin.rationale: Provider origin is receipted explicitly. OpenAI and third-party OpenRouter models remain eligible after disclosure and output controls; Anthropic remains native-only.

matrixReceipt._comment: Receipt contract for model selection. The canonical machine-readable model data lives in plugins/openrouter/skills/openrouter-delegate/references/model-matrix.json; tools/validate-openrouter-cascade.sh rejects drift between that matrix, model-cascade.json quality_rank, and the agentType slugs in this file. Same canonical-with-checked-mirror shape as .security above.
matrixReceipt.statement: Every routing decision recorded in a run receipt must carry matrix_snapshot_date and a one-line rung_rationale naming the deciding axis (cost, context, strength, or availability).

requiredReceiptFields.matrix_snapshot_date: The snapshot_date of the model-matrix.json revision the decision was made against.
requiredReceiptFields.rung_rationale: One line naming the deciding axis for the chosen rung.

matrixReceipt.authority: The matrix recommends, this policy decides, receipts record. A matrix refresh never re-routes anything on its own.
matrixReceipt.rationale: Routing decisions were previously unattributable: the matrix was consumed by nothing at run time, so a receipt could not show which price/context/strength data a rung was chosen against. Naming the snapshot and the deciding axis makes the decision auditable and makes matrix drift visible in the receipt trail.

authorization._comment: How an automated OpenRouter lane becomes authorized. Resolved, never assumed. Ordered, fail-closed: broker-ready retires interim but remains unavailable until broker-owned transport lands; then the interim operator batch is considered only when the broker is absent; otherwise unavailable. Broker presence has THREE states: ready (broker_transport_unavailable), present_not_ready (unknown -- unavailable), and absent (the only state where interim is reachable).

brokerStates.ready: probe parsed with jq -e '.status == "ready"' succeeds -- interim retired, automated dispatch unavailable with reason broker_transport_unavailable until broker-owned transport lands
brokerStates.present_not_ready: client installed but probe errors, is unparseable, or does not report ready -- unknown state, resolves to unavailable with reason broker_present_not_ready; interim mode is withheld
brokerStates.absent: client not installed or not executable -- the only state in which interim_operator_batch is reachable

broker.probe: /usr/local/bin/workflow-authority probe --format json reports status ready, parsed with jq -e '.status == "ready"' and never a substring match
broker.authority: future independent broker-owned run-bound authorization, credential custody, and transport

interim_operator_batch._comment: Deliberate, owner-authorized loosening of approval GRANULARITY -- run-batch instead of per-payload -- not of approval EXISTENCE. Introduced 2026-08-08 because the Linux broker host is unavailable for about two weeks and per-payload interactive approval is too much friction for automated lanes.
interim_operator_batch.programSunsetRationale: About four weeks. The darwin broker milestone is scheduled inside this window. After this date batch files fail validation and extending the program requires a reviewed commit that re-issues the sunset in the schema.
interim_operator_batch.entryRequirement: interactive operator confirmation on the controlling terminal showing each lane's model candidates, provider routing, per-role byte totals, exact digest, and private inspection path; retained request bytes are 0600 and removed after the batch is persisted; no environment variable substitutes for the interactive confirmation
interim_operator_batch.artifactHonesty: The batch file is PROCEDURAL and UNAUTHENTICATED -- bare JSON with no signature, MAC, or user-presence binding. Nothing proves batch-approve or its /dev/tty confirmation ever ran, and a same-user process can hand-write an equivalent file carrying its own digests and the known run id. The confirmation is a control against accidental and automated entry by this tooling, NOT a technical barrier against same-user forgery. Closing that gap is what the out-of-process Workflow Authority Broker does, and it is the primary reason this mode carries a sunset. Do not substitute Keychain ACLs or a shared-secret MAC: same-user enforcement inside a user-readable script is theatre.
interim_operator_batch.transmissionBinding: openrouter-wrapper.sh hashes the exact request envelope it is about to POST and refuses (exit 2) unless the validated schema-v2 batch file's durable lanes mapping binds that lane id to the same digest and model candidates. The bound bytes include model or fallback models, provider routing and sort, streaming options, roles, and ordered message content. The check is at the point of disclosure and does not depend on the lane having run verify-batch first. The private request copy is opened on a dedicated file descriptor, its path is unlinked, its contents are read once into process memory, and curl receives those same in-memory bytes on stdin (--data-binary @-). No path is reopened between digest and POST.
interim_operator_batch.sunsetPinning: All three enforcement layers (payload-authorization.sh PROGRAM_SUNSET, openrouter-wrapper.sh INTERIM_PROGRAM_SUNSET, the dm-review review skill's OPENROUTER_INTERIM_PROGRAM_SUNSET) compare program_sunset against this release constant; a file-asserted future date is not accepted on its own.
interim_operator_batch.retiredWhen: broker probe on the host reports ready
interim_operator_batch.withheldWhen: broker client is installed but does not probe ready (broker_present_not_ready)
interim_operator_batch.retirementMessage: broker available; interim mode retired on this host
interim_operator_batch.nonMatchingPayload: per-payload interactive exact-digest path, else fail closed

unavailable._comment: On hosts with no broker and no valid batch authorization the external rail stays closed and the complete criterion runs on Codex. An available API key, runner, policy, or caller environment variable is not automated dispatch authority.

security._comment: Validated mirror of the OpenRouter-owned delegation policy. The canonical installed-runtime source is plugins/openrouter/skills/openrouter-delegate/references/delegation-security-policy.json. This block keeps pipeline planning self-contained and tools/validate-routing-economics.sh rejects drift.

refuseClasses: explicitly classified private or regulated values
disclosureControls.rationale: Classify the exact outbound bytes. Names of files, directories, headers, variables, vendors, nationalities, and jurisdictions are not disclosure evidence.

reviewControls.rationale: Security-related implementation may be delegated after content and output validation; consequential security completion requires a reviewer family different from the implementer.

intendedLanes: security analysis with independent non-implementing-family sign-off
positiveRouting.rationale: These are the OpenRouter mechanical lanes when exact outbound content passes disclosure controls.
